function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live market feeds, so I can’t tell you the precise spot price of gold right now.  

If you need an up‑to‑date figure, here’s what you can do:

| Source | How to get the price |
|--------|----------------------|
| **Bloomberg** | Visit [bloomberg.com/markets](https://www.bloomberg.com/markets) → “Gold” section. |
| **Reuters** | Go to [reuters.com/finance/commodities/gold](https://www.reuters.com/finance/commodities/gold). |
| **Kitco** | Check [kitco.com/charts/livegold.html](https://kitco.com/charts/livegold.html). |
| **Yahoo Finance** | Search “XAUUSD” or “Gold Spot”. |
| **Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)** | Look at the series *GOLD* for daily prices. |

These sites update their quotes several times per minute during trading hours. If you’re looking for historical trends rather than the exact tick‑by‑tick price, most of them offer downloadable CSV files or interactive charts where you can see the closing price for each day.
